title: qos T2 captures at 1000ms and 65000ms render the same saturated state — the x10 surge is visible only in the T1 drop stream, not in T2 pixels (faithful render, not staleness)
evidence: Measured on the worktree PNGs: 318/921600 differing pixels (0.03%), bbox (634,354)-(728,461); identical 7 packet blobs at identical positions in both frames (size=111 at (341,358),(354,358),(485,526),(498,526),(773,526),(786,526); size=572 at (914,349)). Sim probe (core at this sha, demos/qos.dem seed 3003): '20 1000 24 0 24 20 4 0 24 0 5' vs '1300 65000 20 0 20 16 4 0 20 0 25' (tick ms total delivered on_edge queued inflight laneq0 laneq1 laneq2 drops): the on-pipe picture is the same saturated state (queue at the 4-bundle x lane_queue_packets=6 bound from tick 3); only the drop rate rises (5 -> 25/tick) through the surge.
detail: Drops are spliced out (no drop marker rendered) and the queue is at its bound at both capture instants, so 65000ms.png cannot visually show the surge — that evidence lives in the 1500 re-blessed T1 hashes. Verified faithful: '  PASS qos                 ticks=1500' with rc.ready always true, so the T2 check genuinely compared the blessed PNGs against this sha's render.
recommended_fix: No fix required. Document in the PR body that qos T2 captures show the saturated queue (identical frames) and the surge/contention is pinned by T1 + the drop stream, not T2 pixels.
